original_question: Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), and let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form. Let A be the associated operator on L2(Omega), so that -A generates a bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega). If L-infinity-boundedness means that there exists M > 0 such that ||T(t)f||_infinity <= M ||f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0, can this L-infinity-boundedness property be characterized directly in terms of the sesquilinear form a?
correct_elements: Your draft already targets the right problem almost exactly: the paper’s open problem asks, in the setting of a closed sectorial sesquilinear form a on a dense subspace V of L²(Ω), whether L∞-boundedness of the bounded analytic semigroup generated by the associated operator can be characterized directly in terms of the form a. You also correctly stated the L∞-boundedness property as a uniform estimate ‖T(t)f‖∞ ≤ M‖f‖∞ for f ∈ L²(Ω) ∩ L∞(Ω).
missing_details: The paper explicitly works with complex-valued functions, i.e. V is a dense subspace of L²(Ω; ℂ).
Sectoriality is stated with an angle θ ∈ [0, π/2): for every u ∈ V, one has a(u,u) ∈ Σθ := {z ∈ ℂ \ {0} : |arg z| ≤ θ} ∪ {0}.
Closedness is spelled out as completeness of V for the form norm ‖u‖a := (Re a(u,u) + ‖u‖²L²(Ω))1/2.
The operator A is defined via the standard form representation: u ∈ D(A) and Au = h iff u ∈ V and a(u,v) = ⟨h,v⟩ for all v ∈ V, with the usual L² inner product.
The paper notes that this setup implies that −A generates a bounded analytic semigroup on L²(Ω), in fact contractive on the sector Σπ/2−θ; this is part of the intended scope.
The paper presents this as an open problem, not as a theorem or conjecture with a proposed answer.
The nearby context matters: the special case M = 1 (L∞-contractivity) is already known and is characterized by the Beurling–Deny criterion; your draft omits this orientation point.

The comments also record a sufficient weighted contractivity mechanism involving a function g ∈ L∞(Ω) with g > 0 μ-a.e. and 1/g ∈ L∞(Ω), together with a modified form criterion; this is not the main problem but is part of the exact surrounding context.
refined_question: Let (Ω, μ) be a σ-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L²(Ω; ℂ), and let a: V × V → ℂ be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, linear in the first variable and antilinear in the second, with sectorial angle θ ∈ [0, π/2), meaning a(u,u) ∈ Σθ := {z ∈ ℂ \ {0} : |arg z| ≤ θ} ∪ {0} for all u ∈ V, and with V complete for the norm ‖u‖a := (Re a(u,u) + ‖u‖²L²(Ω))1/2. Let A be the operator on L²(Ω) associated with a in the usual form sense, i.e. u ∈ D(A) and Au = h iff u ∈ V and a(u,v) = ⟨h,v⟩ for all v ∈ V, so that −A generates a bounded analytic semigroup (T(t))t≥0 on L²(Ω). Is there a characterization, stated purely in terms of the sesquilinear form a, of the property that (T(t))t≥0 is L∞-bounded, meaning that there exists M > 0 such that ‖T(t)f‖∞ ≤ M‖f‖∞ for every t ≥ 0 and every f ∈ L²(Ω) ∩ L∞(Ω)?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the paper’s Section 6 open problem on L∞-bounds, and more specifically at Problem 21 rather than the later weighted variants in Problems 22–24. The official formulation is essentially your question, but the paper includes several setup details that should be restored to make it fully stand-alone: the complex L² setting, the precise sectoriality condition via Σθ, the exact form norm defining closedness, and the operator-form correspondence. The paper’s comments show that one should not broaden the target to the already solved M = 1 case (Beurling–Deny) or replace it by the weighted sufficient condition; those are nearby context, not the official target.
